MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  OCTOBER 21, 2025

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:00 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chamber,
  4045 Palos Verdes Drive N, Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR PERSICHINA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Persichina,  Pope,  Ciarolla,  Johnson,
  Holdsworth, Bain and McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST
  19, 2025

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 19, 2025.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  OVERVIEW AND EVALUATION OF PILOT PROGRAM FOR ALL-DAY TENNIS
  CLUB COURT RESERVATIONS AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 21, 2025
   Supervisor Pinuelas gave a presentation regarding the overview and evaluation of
  the pilot program for tennis club court reservations at Ernie Howlett Park (as per
  the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked if the respondents of the survey used the
  courts at the tennis club. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that although it is unknown,
  she believed a general assumption could be made that many of the respondents
  used the courts and played at the tennis club during either reservation time periods
  or during the free use time frames prior to the implementation of the pilot program.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff had
  to intervene at times to respond to conflicts on the pickleball courts. She noted that
  Staff had to clear the pickleball courts prior to the contracted use of the courts due
  to some occasions when players refused to clear the courts. She also stated that
  there were some instances where conflicts would arise between players on the
  pickleball courts.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that the utilization rate appears to be low.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the utilization rate may appear to be low based on
  the courts going to an all-day court reservation style during the pilot program. She
  also stated that Staff received feedback that people were unable to coordinate with
  their groups to reserve a court and preferred the option to just drop-in and see if
  there was anyone playing on the courts.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH asked if Staff knew if tennis club members
  preferred the reservation system during the pilot program. Supervisor Pinuelas
  stated that some members did enjoy the reservation system, but that there were
  some members that preferred drop-in open play regarding pickleball.

  In response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that
  “drop-in open play” in the recommended structure, refers to pickleball as that is
  not a style of play for tennis which is only reservation based. She also noted that
  Staff received feedback from the pickleball community that open play is a popular
  style of play for pickleball.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about the cost recovery of the tennis club
  operations and what the goal of the cost recovery might be. Assistant City Manager
  Davis responded that a cost recovery percentage goal has not been established
  as a fee study is currently underway which will provide further guidance. She noted
  that under the Cost Recovery Policy, recreation programs, such as those outlined
  in the recommended structure for tennis club operations, are not intended to
  generate profit but rather to partially offset operational costs.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 21, 2025
   In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, ACM Davis stated that a partial cost
  recovery model can be applied to the tennis club’s operations under this proposed
  structure.

  COMMISSIONER POPE commented that the pilot program was established to
  help solve a problem, but that it appears that a new problem may have arisen from
  the pilot program and that she appreciates the efforts of Staff and the community
  to find a compromise that works for all parties.

  In response to COMMISSIONER POPE, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that a
  member of the public did not have to have a confirmed group of four in order to
  reserve a court. She gave an example that one person could reserve a court and
  have a group of 15 people join them on their reserved court.

  In response to COMMISSIONER POPE, Supervisor Pinuelas stated some
  pickleball players expressed that it was challenging to coordinate a group to come
  during a specific reservation time. Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the proposed
  new fee-based drop-in open play program accommodates the pickleball player
  who wants the ability to drop-in and join a game without having to plan with a group
  in advance.

  In response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK, Supervisor Pinuelas noted that
  the requirement of a club membership to utilize the courts may present a barrier to
  the standard operations at the tennis club in which both members and non-
  members have access to the courts throughout the day. She also stated that when
  members register, they sign off on a general liability waiver, but the club is open to
  the public and there is not a requirement for a liability waiver to play at the tennis
  club.

  At this time, CHAIR PERSICHINA opened the floor to public comment.

  Laura Patti, Palos Verdes Peninsula resident, expressed concerns about the
  current structure of the pilot program and how it relates to pickleball play. She
  summarized some of the conflict that arose prior to the start of the pilot program.
  She also stated that there is a culture among the pickleball community in which the
  open/drop-in play structure works well for them. She also noted that she is not
  opposed to paying a fee for daily open/drop-in play.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, ACM Davis noted that the court utilization
  table presented in the report referred to weekday afternoon court use during the
  pilot program. She also stated that the intent of the pilot program was not to be a
  permanent solution but a temporary program to better understand how the courts
  were being used. She noted that Staff realized that the pilot program structure was

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 21, 2025
   restrictive and that there was less usage which is why the proposed hybrid
  schedule is being recommended.

  Michelle Grajeda, Lomita resident, expressed concern about the current structure
  of the pilot program and how it relates to pickleball play. She stated that the
  proposed hybrid structure was confusing. She also stated that it may be more
  effective and efficient to offer a full afternoon of fee-based open/drop-in play for
  the pickleball courts from noon to dusk. She also stated that she enjoys both the
  reservation system and the open/drop-in play system and feels that there is an
  opportunity to satisfy the entire community.

  In response to Ms. Grajeda, Staff noted that the pickleball courts have not been
  reserved consistently throughout the afternoon during the pilot program.

  In response to Ms. Grajeda, CHAIR PERSICHINA stated that recommendation
  made that evening by the Commission would be presented to the City Council for
  final approval.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked Ms. Grajeda for clarification regarding her
  recommendation of play. Ms. Grajeda confirmed that she would prefer a simpler
  schedule, in which the fee-based open/drop-in pickleball play would be available
  the entire afternoon on two or three days a week.

  Ernie Bumatay, Rolling Hills Estates resident, stated he is a long-standing member
  of the tennis club. He noted that whatever was decided should represent the
  satisfaction of the community. He also stated that tennis participation has dropped
  off since the pilot program started. He requested that the system established be
  simple and consistent.

  Andy Whitty, Redondo Beach resident, expressed concerns about the current
  structure of the pilot program and how it relates to pickleball play. He stated there
  was no conversation between Staff and the pickleball community prior to a decision
  regarding the implementation of the pilot program. He stated that there needed to
  be more transparency regarding the complaints and conflicts on the pickleball
  courts. He stated that he was not opposed to the hybrid structure presented for
  reservation use and open/drop-in play. He stated that he felt most of the use was
  from community use pickleball play compared to open use play.

  In response to COMMISSIONER POPE, Mr. Whitty clarified that the difference
  between community play and open play is that in community play there is a
  communication email thread between groups to communicate when to meet to play
  on the courts during a certain time frame, whereas open/drop-in play is a structured
  time frame for drop-in instead of the courts being freely available for use at any
  time.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 21, 2025
   COMMISSIONER BAIN asked Mr. Whitty to clarify how they properly divide up use
  of the courts for community games when many people show up to play. Mr. Whitty
  stated that when members of the community group show up, they jump in and
  begin to play a game. He also noted that when a member of the public that was
  not part of the community group showed up to the courts, the group would be
  accepting of them and have them join in the play.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked Mr. Whitty whether the ability to play within
  the community group or in an open play format conflicts with the reservation
  system. He responded that you could start with a group of four players on one
  court and then more people would come and join in the play and merge onto the
  other three courts. He stated that after a few hours there could be many players
  migrating in and migrating out to use the courts.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked Mr. Whitty if he was opposed to a fee-based
  open/drop-in play program. He responded that he did not have any opposition to
  a fee-based structure for the open/drop-in play program but stated it doesn’t offer
  the opportunity to continue community group play.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH asked Mr. Whitty if having a member of the
  community group reserve one or more courts at a set time, allowing others from
  the group to drop in during that time, could help address some of the issues raised.
  Mr. Whitty responded that it is what is occurring to some extent, but the community
  group typically reserves a court only when four players are confirmed, and
  additional members may join if they are available.

  Ms. Wendy Wu, Palos Verdes Peninsula resident, commented that community
  play and open play are the styles of play that work best for the pickleball
  community. She stated that she is a member of the tennis club and has been
  making reservations during the pilot program. She also stated that she discovered
  the pickleball courts because of the community play available prior to the pilot
  program. She also stated that she would not have any issues with fee-based
  open/drop-in play and agreed with Ms. Grajeda that the proposed hybrid structure
  was a bit confusing and that a more simplified consistent schedule would work
  best.

  In response to COMMISSIONER BAIN, Ms. Grajeda clarified that she is a
  volunteer with the City and has run the City’s open play pickleball program on
  Monday and Friday evenings from April through October since the overlays were
  installed to better introduce pickleball to the community.

  A discussion ensued between the Commission and Staff regarding Staff’s
  recommendations and the public comments made during the meeting in order to

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 21, 2025
   develop a modified recommendation on a proposed hybrid structure for afternoon
  hours.

  The Commission came to a consensus to recommend continuing weekday
  afternoon staffing at the Tennis Club.

  VICE CHAIR POPE  made  a  motion,  seconded  by  COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  RECOMMEND THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONTINUING WEEKDAY
  AFTERNOON STAFFING AT THE TENNIS CLUB TO SUPPORT
  ONGOING FACILITY MANAGEMENT AND PROGRAMMING.

  AYES:  Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth, Bain, McCormick, Pope, and
  Persichina
  ABSENT:  None

  The Commission continued to discuss the proposed hybrid structure for weekday
  court management presented in the staff report. A consensus was made to make
  changes to the proposed structure based on the feedback received.

  The Commission proposed and recommended the City Council approve the
  following hybrid structure for weekday court management:

  •  Mondays from 12:00 PM to dusk would be designated for paid pickleball
  open/drop-in play ($5 per person) and paid tennis reservations.

  •  Tuesdays from 12:00 PM to 3:00 PM would be designated for paid pickleball
  open/drop-in play ($5 per person) and tennis reservations. There would be
  contracted use from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM and paid reservations from 6:00
  PM to dusk during the months of contracted use. When not in contracted
  use, there would be paid reservations for pickleball and tennis from 3:00
  PM to dusk (court use from 3:00 PM to dusk will be assessed to determine
  the best option for that time frame when not in contract use for the future,
  with the option to either keep as a reservation only time or to open up more
  hours for paid pickleball open/drop-in play).
  •  Wednesdays from 12:00 PM to dusk would be designated for paid pickleball
  open/drop-in play ($5 per person) and paid tennis reservations.

  •  Thursdays from 12:00 PM to 3:00 PM would be designated for paid
  pickleball open/drop-in play ($5 per person) and paid tennis reservations.
  Contracted use will take place from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM and paid
  reservations from 6:00 PM to dusk during the months of contracted use.
  When not in contracted use, there will be paid reservations for pickleball
  and tennis from 3:00 PM to dusk (court use from 3:00 PM to dusk will be
  assessed to determine the best option for that time frame when not in

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 21, 2025
   contract use for the future, with the option to either keep as a reservation
  only time or to open up more hours for paid pickleball open/drop-in play).

  •  Fridays from 12:00 PM to close would be designated for free pickleball
  open/drop-in play and free tennis court use.

  The Commission proposed and recommended the City Council approve a fee of
  $5 per person as the rate for the pickleball open/drop-in play periods.

  AYES:  Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth, Bain, McCormick, Pope, and
  Persichina
  ABSENT:  None

  6.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  NOVEMBER AND DECEMBER MEETING DATES (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas informed the Commission that the Council Chambers would
  not be available on the regular meeting dates of Tuesday, November 18 and
  Tuesday, December 16. She stated that Staff is proposing alternative special
  meeting dates of Wednesday, November 12 or Wednesday, November 19 and
  Monday, December 15 or Wednesday, December 17. The Commission conferred
  and determined that Wednesday, November 12 and Wednesday, December 17
  worked best for the alternate special meeting dates.

  B.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided an update regarding the upcoming Peninsula
  Parade of Lights event scheduled for Saturday, December 6 at 6:00 pm. He gave
  details regarding the grand marshal and community grand marshal, updates
  regarding the marketing and reported that the parade application is available
  online. He also provided information regarding the pre-parade reception at El Polla
  Inka.

  C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.
